name: rotator cuff disease overview
title: Rotator cuff disease: pain, weakness and restricted motion; examine active against passive motion, the impingement signs (Neer, Hawkins, painful arc) and cuff strength; then stage it by how far the tendon has gone: stage I (shoulder impingement syndrome) inflamed but intact, stage II partial-thickness and stage III full-thickness defects, and rotator cuff arthropathy with the humerus riding up to the acromion; nonoperative care first at every stage, then surgery by stage when pain persists, the shoulder is weak or it followed an acute injury

root.title: Rotator cuff disease: how far has the TENDON gone?
lines: most common shoulder disorder · onset in the 40s · progressive
INTRINSIC (usual): vascularity · tension overload · tendon degeneration

pres.title: Examine the shoulder
lines: impingement signs: NEER · HAWKINS · PAINFUL ARC

rows: Nonoperative, every stage: enough in the MAJORITY
education · activity modification · pain management (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs)
SURGERY when: pain persists · weakness · after an acute injury
